measurer_summary.lens: Phase A6 raw-field census: every key path in every source, flagged as TIMER, CLOCK, COUNTER, HASH_ID, STATUS or TOKEN; marked captured or uncaptured against ir.py COLUMNS plus cc_jsonl extra; with a non-tool entry inventory and 5 pre-specified redundancy identities

observations.statement: In Claude Code logs, the harness's Read counter toolUseResult.file.numLines equals the number of line-numbered lines in the text the model sees. This holds in both swechat and cc_local.
observations.numbers: swechat 2510/2514 = 0.998, Wilson [0.996, 0.999], cluster 0.998 [0.997, 1.0] over 149 files, 4 files mismatch. Mismatch diffs (text minus numLines), n=4: min -2312, median -1595, max -1. cc_local 191/194 = 0.985, Wilson [0.956, 0.995], 59 files, all 3 diffs -1.
observations.mechanical_explanation: Both fields are written by the same harness from the same read, so this is internal redundancy, not an independent witness. The 4 large negative mismatches may be truncated or persisted outputs (unverified).

observations.statement: A subagent's totalToolUseCount (Agent/Task toolUseResult) equals the number of distinct nested tool_use ids in its agent_progress traffic.
observations.numbers: 190/190 = 1.0, Wilson [0.980, 1.0], 71 files. A further 94 results in 20 files have no nested traffic, so they could not be checked.
observations.mechanical_explanation: The harness counts the same stream it writes, so this is redundancy, not independence.

candidate_mechanisms.name: Structured-counter vs visible-text recount
candidate_mechanisms.measurement: For each tool result, recount the quantity from the model-visible text or the call arguments and compare it to the harness counter by exact equality, pre-registered. Honest baseline I4: 2510/2514 (swechat) and 191/194 (cc_local). Rewritten or fabricated result text should break the equality unless the counter is rewritten too.
candidate_mechanisms.false_positive_source: Truncated or persisted-to-file outputs, system reminders appended to result text, line-number formatting changes across harness versions, and Read calls with an offset or limit.
candidate_mechanisms.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED: I don't know of published work that uses the harness's structured copy of a tool result as a cross-check. Agent-observability tools may do this already.

candidate_mechanisms.name: Second-clock duration consistency
candidate_mechanisms.measurement: Check that each harness timer is at most the gap between the surrounding event clocks (call to end, turn start to end), with a tolerance set from an honest baseline before any outcome is examined. A reported duration longer than the wall-clock gap, or a gap with no possible execution time, would flag a result that was not produced by execution.
candidate_mechanisms.false_positive_source: Parallel tool calls, clocks written at flush time rather than event time, millisecond granularity, skew between processes, and backgrounded commands.
candidate_mechanisms.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED: duration-vs-timestamp checks are standard in log forensics. Applying them to agent tool logs may be less common.

candidate_mechanisms.name: file-history-snapshot mutation reconciliation
candidate_mechanisms.measurement: For each successful Edit or Write on path P at time t, expect a later snapshot to show a version bump for P with backupTime >= t. Count claimed edits that have no bump, and bumps that have no claimed edit.
candidate_mechanisms.false_positive_source: Snapshots are per user message, so edits coalesce. Paths outside the tracked set are missing. About 19% of files have no snapshot at all. Resumed sessions and Bash-made edits also break the mapping.
candidate_mechanisms.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED: this harness record seems unused in the literature I know of.

candidate_mechanisms.name: Session-tally recount
candidate_mechanisms.measurement: Recompute each tally from the transcript (usage sums, tool counts, patch line sums) and compare. Report the disagreement rate with a session-clustered CI.
candidate_mechanisms.false_positive_source: Tallies derived from the same transcript agree tautologically. Resumed or compacted sessions change the totals. Subagent tokens may be included in one count and not the other.

candidate_mechanisms.name: Cumulative counter chain
candidate_mechanisms.measurement: Check the chain identity total(n) = total(n-1) + last(n), and that ordinal counters only increase. Honest baseline I1b: 0.970, with breaks in 5/26 files.
candidate_mechanisms.false_positive_source: Counter resets at compaction, rollback or resume, which plausibly explain the observed breaks (unverified).

candidate_mechanisms.name: Nested-subagent tally check
grounded_in: CC toolUseResult.totalToolUseCount / totalTokens / totalDurationMs (captured in extra)
cc_local workflow.json totalToolCalls vs subagent JSONL
candidate_mechanisms.measurement: Compare the parent's reported subagent tallies with a recount of the nested or sidecar subagent transcript. Baseline I5: 190/190.
candidate_mechanisms.false_positive_source: Nesting is absent in current Claude Code (cc_local), and subagent files can be missing or truncated.

candidate_mechanisms.name: External git witness of claimed edits
candidate_mechanisms.measurement: Match the agent-claimed patch hunks to the committed diff, and report the fraction of claimed hunks that never reach a commit.
candidate_mechanisms.false_positive_source: Human edits between agent and commit, squashed or rebased commits, and work that was never committed. Another lens (phase_c_commit_witness) may already cover this.

candidate_mechanisms.name: AI Village dual record of model calls
candidate_mechanisms.measurement: Join an event to its turn and compare usage and the action between the two tables.
candidate_mechanisms.false_positive_source: Events exist only for some action types, the join key is uncertain, and created_at is a row-insert time that can lag the event.

could_not_measure: village-transcript.json (one 362 MB JSON document, a rendering of events and chat_messages) was not censused.
Agreement of the uncaptured second clocks and timers with event timestamps: the fields are listed, but no duration-vs-gap check was run.
file-history-snapshot vs Edit/Write reconciliation: the fields are listed, not measured.
Whether the loaders actually ingest the uncaptured fields. The loader mark is only a string-literal match on analysis/loaders/*.py, which other agents are editing; the caches were not read.

Fill rates of key paths deeper than the depth limits (4 for transcripts and cc_local, 3 for table JSON columns, 3 or 6 for AI Village), and of cc_local subtrees hidden for privacy (user-defined schemas, non-builtin tool inputs and results).
Swechat transcript key-path fill rates cover only the 300-file stratified sample. The entry-type inventory covers the full population.
Copilot (2 files) and simple_text (4 files) are too small for rates.
1 OpenCode transcript failed JSON parsing and was not censused (no salvage).
conversations.content: only 340 of 500 sampled non-null rows parsed as JSON.
AI Village computer_use_turns CIs are Wilson over rows. The head spans 17,418 distinct sessions, so no session clustering was applied.
OpenCode's actual token-total formula: by design, nothing beyond the 2 pre-specified formulas was tried.

verifier.lens: raw_census (Phase A6). I re-derived every check with my own code, writing only to scratchpad. All of my numbers are in C:\Users\Prathik\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\C--Swarms\5b3cb362-197f-4ccc-a976-2d9bb1ddbc1a\scratchpad\rederive_raw_census.json. The scripts that produced them sit in the same folder: rd_swechat.py, agg_swechat.py, rd_other.py, rd_cc_local.py, rd_tables.py, rd_aiv.py and diag_*.py. I used the lens's own 300-file swechat sample list to match its n, then reran every check on the full population. The cc_local outputs are aggregate counts only. Only after I had my numbers did I read the lens script, to explain the differences. My prompt cut O17 off mid-sentence, so I checked the events-table fields from the notes.

checks.my_numbers: Swechat sample matches exactly: 2510/2514 = 0.9984, Wilson [0.9959, 0.9994], cluster [0.9970, 1.0] over 149 files; 4 mismatching files; diffs -2312 to -1. The 4 are 3 persisted-output previews and 1 case with numLines=1 and no numbered text lines (L=0). Full swechat population: 87827/88229 = 0.9954, Wilson [0.9950, 0.9959], cluster [0.9947, 0.9960] over 4603 files; 275 mismatching files; 402 diffs from -3464 to -1, median -1140. All 402 mismatches are harness or dataset formats: 282 '<\persisted-output>' previews, 105 'file shorter than offset' warnings, 7 '<identical to result [rN]...>' references, 7 redacted contents and 1 negative line numbers. None is unexplained. cc_local main sessions, full: 570/578 = 0.986, Wilson [0.973, 0.993], cluster [0.976, 0.994] over 182 files; all 8 mismatches are empty-file warnings with diff -1. In cc_local subagent files, 0 of 12 Read results carry numLines.
checks.problem: The sample understates the mismatch rate: the full-population rate 0.9954 lies below the sample's cluster CI [0.997, 1.0]. The 'unverified' explanation is now verified: every mismatch is a harness display format (persisted preview, warning, dedup reference) or dataset redaction. A detector would therefore have to whitelist these formats. 'Holds in cc_local' covers main sessions only; subagent files carry no Read numLines.

checks.my_numbers: Sample matches exactly: 190/190, Wilson [0.980, 1.0], 71 files; 94 results in 20 files have no nested traffic. Full population: 6623/6623, Wilson [0.9994, 1.0], 1934 files. Uncheckable: 2150 results in 634 files, which is 2150/8773 = 0.245 [0.236, 0.254] of Agent/Task results. The uncheckable results have a median totalToolUseCount of 21, so they are not trivially empty.
checks.problem: The JSON stores the uncheckable set as I5_cc_agent_toolcount_no_nested_traffic with match 94, n 94, rate 1.0 and a Wilson CI. The code calls add(True), so a non-check is encoded as a 100% pass. It should be a bare count. The statement itself words this correctly. A quarter of Agent results cannot be checked.

The lens's own flagged[] marks these paths loader_pair or loader_leaf. Only hookInfos[].durationMs, and info.time.completed outside message-error events, are really dropped. AI Village updated_at is a copy of the row-insert time, not an independent clock.

checks.my_numbers: Counts match exactly. I1a: 1935/1950, 2 files, diffs 19480 to 601429. I1b: 1862/1919, cluster [0.941, 0.994] over 26 files, 5 files mismatching, 57 diffs from -601429 to -19480. Full population: I1a 16015/16106, 24 files mismatching; I1b 15302/15917 = 0.961, cluster [0.952, 0.973] over 173 files, 39 files mismatching. The total decreases in 0/57 sample breaks and 0/615 full breaks. Instead total_token_usage equals the previous event's in every break, so each diff is just -last(n). 45/57 sample breaks (531/615 full) are exact duplicate token_count events, with the whole info block equal to the previous one. After dropping consecutive duplicates, the chain holds 1862/1874 in the sample and 15302/15386 in the full population. The remaining 12 sample breaks (84 full) have a flat total and a nonzero last. 12/12 of them (81/84 full) come right after a compacted or thread_rolled_back event, and only these match the I1a magnitudes.
checks.problem: The direction claim is wrong. The total never 'jumps down'; it stays flat. Mechanical causes explain every break: re-emitted duplicate token_count events (45/57) and post-compaction/rollback accounting (12/57). This should be classed artifact, not surprise. 'Magnitudes matching' holds for only 12 of 57 breaks.

checks.my_numbers: Matches exactly. F1: 148/633 = 0.234, Wilson [0.203, 0.268], cluster [0.106, 0.381], 46 files. F2: 12/633. Mismatch diffs n=485, min -8947, median -71, max -8. Full population: F1 3155/14854 = 0.212; F2 255/14854. checks.problem: The null as stated is correct. However, the post-hoc fit shows that the total simply excludes reasoning. The null reflects the choice of pre-specified formula; it is not evidence that OpenCode lacks a token identity. Read it as 'formula misspecified', not 'no redundancy'.
